title: Implement DVB-T2 bit interleaving (column-row)
description:
## Goal

Implement the DVB-T2 column-row (block) bit interleaver from ETSI
EN 302 755 v1.4.1 §6.1.3 in
`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/bit_interleaver.rs` (or under
`crates/gf2-coding/src/modem/`, at the implementer's choice).
This is the deterministic, frame-aware, MODCOD-dependent interleaver
that sits between LDPC encoding and QAM mapping.

It is distinct from the random-seed `BitInterleaver` in
`crates/gf2-coding/src/fading.rs` (around line 509), which is for
generic decorrelation, not standards-compliant DVB-T2.

## Context

EN 302 755 §6.1.3 defines a two-stage permutation:

1. Bit interleaving inside an FECFRAME using a column-row block
   interleaver whose dimensions (Nc, Nr) depend on FECFRAME size,
   modulation order, and code rate. Bits are written column by
   column and read row by row.
2. For 16-QAM and 64-QAM, a column-twist offset is applied per
   column before reading; the twist offsets are tabulated in the
   spec (Table 9 / Table 9a).

This task implements both stages forward and inverse, plus an
LLR-domain inverse for the receive path.

## Deliverables

1. Public type, e.g. `DvbT2BitInterleaver`, with at minimum:
   - `pub fn new(modcod: DvbT2Modcod) -> Self`
   - `pub fn interleave(&self, bits: &BitVec) -> BitVec`
   - `pub fn deinterleave(&self, bits: &BitVec) -> BitVec`
   - `pub fn deinterleave_llrs(&self, llrs: &[Llr]) -> Vec<Llr>`
2. `DvbT2Modcod` parameter struct that selects (Nc, Nr, twist[]) from
   the spec for the in-scope configurations × {16-QAM, 64-QAM}.
3. Unit tests:
   - roundtrip identity on random inputs across all in-scope modcods,
   - word-boundary edge cases (0, 1, 63, 64, 65 bits beyond a
     multiple of the column dimension),
   - LLR-domain inverse correctness via index-tagging.

## Success criteria

- [hard] Roundtrip identity: `deinterleave(interleave(x, m), m) == x`
  for random inputs across all 3 in-scope rates × {16-QAM, 64-QAM}.
- [hard] LLR-domain inverse: feeding interleaved-then-noisy LLRs back
  through `deinterleave_llrs` yields LLRs in the same order as the
  original pre-interleaved bit sequence (verified by index-tagging
  test).
- [hard] The interleaver is consumed end-to-end by the TP07a vector
  validation in 4cdaf1c5 — that validation passes.
- [hard] No new `unsafe`; satisfies `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.
- [hard] Public API has standard rustdoc (description, arguments,
  examples that compile, panics, complexity).

## Spec reference

ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1 §6.1.3 ("Bit interleaver") and Tables 9 / 9a
for the column-twist values.
